works.

The Scribe created the archive to seal the cards forever and keep the balance of the world.

core design principles are shown on

●

The first 100 levels are to teach the player
all the core gameplay values and strategies
they can form.
Make levels that either rewards mastery or
speed. Make sure to rotate between them
sufficiently for gameplay variety.
Monochromatic and texture heavy levels
should reward speed, whereas levels where
either an item or zombie is being introduced
should reward mastery instead should be a
“no brainer” level.
The approaches can be combined after level
100.

●
●

●
❖
❖
❖
●

Don’t match approaches back to back too
much.
Don’t match more than 2 until level 200
Match 3 sparingly after level 200.
The levels solution should be obvious in the
first glance. That’s not to say levels should
be easy, it just means, on the first look, the
strategy should be obvious, especially for
the first 100 levels. We’ll confuse players
later on after d7 levels by introducing nonobvious levels or trick strategy levels so in
early levels, please avoid these kind of
tricks.

How To Use
Colors?

We have 4 types of color levels. Levels should try to
adhere to these types or use lighter monster track if
using a combination of multiple.

Monochrome
●

●
●
●
●

When making monochrome levels, use objects of the same color that has
at least one other color or detail that’s in another color. Pure color items
are okay, but they shouldn’t exceed 2-3 and should be still visually
distinguishable via shape or texture.
Use monochrome levels sparingly and make sure to rotate between colors.
When making monochromatic levels make sure you choose a middle
saturation unless some textures make it okay to go higher or lower.
Players take a longer time to solve a monochrome level so make sure to
compensate with a more forgiving monster track.
Try to follow with a more forgiving level after a monochromatic level. Aim
to follow up with a level that has items distinguishable through shape and
texture (e.g. like a ball level). At the very least, try to change up the
gameplay style focus.

Complementary Color
Usage
●

When players look at a level made out of complementary colors, they will perceive it as a
whole. Use this to to the levels advantage to steer players towards a certain color via texture

●
●

●

and saturation.
This type of level will get hard in the middle. So make sure your monster track intensifies or
decrease monster track difficulty based on the level difficulty you want. Levels after 70ish are
eligible to support an increase in the middle rhythm in a complementary color level.
Distribution of colors doesn’t really matter. If you have equal amount of the colors, player will
gravitate towards texture and saturation. Same is true if one color is less dominant, therefore
looking more prominent on top of it’s complementary counterpart. Use forced tops and
bottoms if you are concerned about preventing abuse.
Good practice is to use items and details of various sizes for each color. Otherwise the level
will be unfairly difficult and luck will play too much role. If your goal is to create more rhythm
towards the end, you can use similar items but I recommend you force them bottom to create
a nice gameplay shift and layer

.

Analogue
Levels
●
●
●
●
●

Analogue levels are a great alternative to monochrome levels and allow for more flexibility in
item selection.
Analogue levels items should be more or less split equally between colors. If There

is an

imbalance, unlike the complimentary levels, the level will always be a lot more easier.
Analogue levels are great for using the same item of different colors.
If you go for three analogue colors, the third color, either the left one or the right one needs
to become an accent color and have less objects in that color. If you want accent items
without adding another color, go for texture accents.
Neutral colors can always be used as an alternative to a third analogue.

Texture
accent

Example of third
analogue being an
accent

Triad and Tetrad
Levels
●
●
●
●
●

Triad and Tetrad levels should be considered when a noisy level is required for variety.
They can use any triad and tetrad combination and include a neutral, but sparingly.
Neutrals shouldn’t include items the same color as the triad or the tetrad. So if a red shuriken
is present, a gray shuriken shouldn’t be in the level. So it should be avoided in general, but
okay to use sparingly.
Make sure to use textures in such levels.
Use these levels if you want to create levels with similar size items.

Experimental
Levels

●
●

Here is an example of an experimental level. It combines a monochrome level with a texture
challenge.
Feel free to throw this kind of level in the funnel to see player reaction for readiness for
mechanic combination etc.
If you have this type of experimental level, make sure it falls in the middle of well learned
passive skills. For example make a level like this after introducing monochromatic levels and
texture challenge levels and There

The Role of Rhythm in Level Making
●
●
●
●
●

A good level should have a rhythm unique to that level. And a good curve should include variety of level rhythms.
For casual games, avoid using rhythm curves that start fast and slow down over time. Unless you catch a fun one, start slow
and build into it.
The core principle of using rhythm in level making is to make sure the player falls into repetitive motion and gets zoned
out/relaxed while engaging with the content. So as long as this is achieved, your rhythm is working.
Since we’re working with CPM, you can easily test your methods with the level design bot.
You can use rhythm via objects or the monsters, both will work

.

Item Rhythm

●

A good level should have a rhythm unique to that
level. And a good curve should include variety of
level rhythms.

Monster Rhythm
●

A good level should have a rhythm unique to that
level. And a good curve should include variety of
level rhythms.

Core Progression Principles
●

The main principle of the level progression is subjecting players to a certain CPM, and failing
them if they don’t match the speed required.
This requirement begins at very low CPMs until the core game learning curve levels are passed and then
progressively becomes harder, capping at a CPM that will be determined by the data later but projected
to land at 100-120 CPM as a plateau.
As a secondary target, the level durations should also curve and increase over time, eventually reaching
the cap of 90-120 seconds based on the objects of a level.

●
●

Other Considerations
●
●
●

The levels should have zombies reaching the cannon at the target CPM. The logic being, if the players

falls short of the CPM the zombies would pile at the cannon and create urgency.
Try to put zombies at exact times to make sure to achieve this effect, especially in levels that have area
affect items to ensure easier balance.
Level balance target is for players to finish a level without cards, winstreaks, or boosters at
the target CPM.

Levels 25-40 → 45 seconds
Levels 40-75 → 60 seconds

Levels 150-onward → 90-120 seconds.

Item Targets

with occasional

multicolor levels or 4 for item intro
levels.

retention data endures the

record.body_text:
General Rule Chart
| Mechanic | Rewind? | Source | Gray Out? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core Loop | Yes | [PERSON_NAME_0550] | No |
| Special Tiles | No | [PERSON_NAME_0550] | Yes |
| Boosters | No | [PERSON_NAME_0550] | Yes |
| Character Skills | Yes | [PERSON_NAME_0550] | Yes |
| Tutorials | Yes | Tutorial Editor | No (Hide UI) |
| Objectives | Yes | [PERSON_NAME_0550] | No |
| Streaks | Yes | [PERSON_NAME_0550] | No |
| Tokens | Yes | [PERSON_NAME_0550] | No |
Core Loop
Core Loop means the very basics of the game, meaning matching and drawing. The core loop is rewindable. Mega tile counts within the core loop.
Special Tiles
Special Tiles are the advanced mechanics in the game that change the properties of normal tiles. Vanishing tiles, bomb tiles, etc are examples of special tiles.
When the player interacts with a special tile, the rewind button will go gray and players cannot interact with rewind until they return to the core mechanic.
Exception! The vanishing tile will go to its previous color if rewinded.
Boosters

Currently, we have 3 boosters in the game.
Bomb: Turns a random normal tile into a bomb tile.
+3 Cards: Allows players to add 3 more cards to their deck.
Wildcard: Turns a deck tile into a golden tile that allows any match.
! Rewind exception: A wildcard is not rewindable if it’s acquired as a booster. However, if it comes from a character skill or streak reward, it will be rewindable and the tile will return to deck as intended.
Character Skills
Each character has special abilities and we call these character skills.
Characters have passive skills that activate before a level starts. Therefore, rewind will start grayed out, and after the core loop starts with a match or draw, the rewind button will be usable.
Tutorials
Rewind will be hidden from the board for the duration of any tutorial.
Objectives
Level objectives are displayed in the pre-level dialogue as well as within the game. Players must complete these objectives to earn 2 or 3 stars.
We have 4 types of objectives
Longstreak: Everytime player makes a match the counter goes up.
Cards Left: Player must complete the level with the predetermined number of cards.
vanishing: Players must match vanishing tiles to complete a level with more starts.
Bomb: Players must use bomb tiles to complete a level with more stars.
Each of these elements use a dynamic UI. When rewind is used, this UI will need to increase and decrease in number where applicable.
Streaks
When player uses a rewind, the current streak status will go down one step. If the move that needs to be rewinded is a streak compilation, the reward will be returned.
Tokens
Tokens will be rewindable. If the player has more than 1 token the counter will go down one number. If they have one number the token will simply disappear. The character tile that provided the token will be returned to the board as usual.
What will happen to the character token tile???
Rewind UI and Gold Rule
Rewind will be rewarded to players throughout the game. If they have unused rewinds, the UI will display the number of rewinds available to the player. If the player is out of rewinds, the rewind price will be listed instead and the players may buy rewind at any time with their in-game gold.

record.body_text:
Train Level Design Guidelines
Prefab Selection
There are some things to consider when selecting prefabs for optimal train movement and player engagement.
Make sure the prefab tile count isn’t too much. The levels are more fun when the train is constantly moving. So even when hardcode allows for fast solving keep the prefab pieces to 3-5 range.
If you want to use a prefab with more tiles make sure it’s vertically melting away both by layout design and hardcode.
Although horizontal pieces have their place and are fun within the train levels, use them to pace the level. Remember, every time you use a horizontal piece, you’re essentially stopping the train and making the player focus anywhere from 3-5 seconds. Use it wisely and when necessary. Using them as breaks or obstacles is acceptable if it’s not overdone.
2. Camera Considerations
For camera considerations, use the markers effectively, and take advantage of the [PERSON_NAME_0550]’s marker logic. The goal is to show the player the upcoming pieces, so they have a sense of progression and know what more is coming. We never want the train to jerk off and move suddenly. The feeling we give to players should be that they are constantly matching away to unlock the train’s way.
Be careful about face-up tiles
To avoid bugs and cheating, make sure your face-up tiles do not reveal themselves half way. There is no right or wrong way to do it but I find placing a marker a bit below than the prefab does the trick. Make sure you playtest the level until you’re completely happy with the marker placement.
Observe the marker and open tile border in these screenshots .
Don’t use too frequent markers
Placing the markers too frequently leads to excessive camera movement which it’s motion sickness triggering. If they are too close to each other, even matching the tiles in a horizontal cluster can move the camera 3 times.
Then observe the in game implications here.
